content.user_title: Write Cold Emails With Evidence and Sending Checks
content.value_statement: Generic outreach and weak sender authentication can undermine email campaigns. This skill combines sourced personalization, concise follow-ups, public DNS diagnostics, and numeric stop rules.
actual_capabilities: Research public recipient signals and record their dates, sources, and relevance without inventing personalization.
Draft a short first email and two or three follow-ups with distinct angles, sender identity, and opt-out language.
Query public MX, SPF, DMARC, and selector-specific DKIM records with the bundled shell script using dig or host.
Review sender reputation, volume, warm-up, unsubscribe requirements, and content in a defined order.
Propose numeric stop rules for bounces, complaints, replies, opt-outs, and mailbox volume.
Use connected Revnu tools to prepare outreach, manage explicit review decisions, retrieve results, and suppress recipients within account permissions.
limitations: DNS records do not prove authentication passes on sent messages or guarantee inbox placement, replies, or meetings.
DNS checks require compatible lookup tools; public research requires browsing access, and missing evidence must remain unverified.
Without connected sending tools, the output is a snapshot and does not schedule emails, monitor campaigns, or enforce stop rules.
Revnu automation requires a connected paid service; provider requirements and regional legal obligations need current verification.

use_cases.title: Prepare founder outreach
use_cases.description: Create a sourced first email and follow-up sequence for a small prospect list, with checks and limits before manual sending.

use_cases.title: Investigate delivery problems
use_cases.description: Review domain authentication before copy, identify volume or reputation concerns, and document evidence and required fixes.

use_cases.title: Review connected campaigns
use_cases.description: Inspect Revnu review items, apply explicit sending decisions, check outreach results, and suppress recipients who opt out.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a cold email and two follow-ups for [buyer role] at [company]. Our product solves [problem]. Use only [approved proof]. Do not send anything. Ask for missing sender details before preparing final signatures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare outreach from a short product brief.

prompt_templates.title: Add verified recipient context
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [recipient companies] for dated public signals relevant to [product]. Cite the source and date for each signal. State when no dated signal exists. Draft one sequence per company without invented observations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: personalize outreach using verifiable research.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose domain readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [sending domain] using DKIM selector [selector]. We send [daily volume] from [mailbox count] mailboxes created [date]. Report exact DNS evidence, unchecked items, unsubscribe gaps, and numeric stop rules. Do not change DNS or send messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate delivery risk before launching a campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare connected outreach
prompt_templates.prompt: With my connected Revnu account, prepare outreach to [authorized segment] using [approved proof]. Apply [sending limits] and [stop rules]. Prepare the sequence for review. Confirm my account approval settings before delegation. Do not send, connect accounts, or purchase anything without my explicit decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a connected campaign with explicit approval boundaries.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: write an opening paragraph for clinic operations leads about scheduling across sites. No dated public signal or customer proof is available.
output_examples.output: Reason to write: no dated signal found. Opening paragraph: Coordinating schedules across clinics can leave operations teams reconciling changes by hand. Is keeping site schedules consistent a problem for your team? Proof: omitted because none was supplied. Sent: nothing.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: propose campaign stop rules and summarize readiness when DNS checks cannot run.
output: Authentication: not checked because DNS lookup tools are unavailable. Obtain lookup output and verify authentication on a real test message.
Proposed bounce rule: pause when hard bounces reach 2% in a batch of at least 50 messages.
Proposed complaint rule: pause when the reported daily spam rate reaches 0.1%.
Any reply stops follow-ups; any opt-out requires immediate suppression. These defaults need approval. Sent: nothing.

best_practices: Provide approved proof, real sender details, and source links; keep uncertain claims outside email bodies.
Verify public DNS results against authentication headers on a real test message and recheck current provider requirements.
Agree numeric stop rules and review connected approval settings before authorizing sending.
anti_patterns: Inventing recipient events, customer results, identities, or misleading reply-style subject lines.
Splitting volume across deceptive domains or manufacturing engagement to evade provider limits.
Treating DNS publication, open counts, or missing metrics as proof of successful delivery or buyer interest.

faq.question: Do I need a Revnu account?
faq.answer: No. Drafting, research, and checks can work without an account, subject to available tools. Optional automation requires a connected paid service.

faq.question: Does the skill send emails?
faq.answer: The standalone workflow drafts without sending. Connected Revnu tools can send real email under account approval settings and explicit review decisions.

faq.question: What does the domain checker inspect?
faq.answer: It queries public MX, SPF, DMARC, and DKIM records using dig or host. It does not modify DNS or authenticate to mailboxes.

faq.question: What happens if no recipient signal is found?
faq.answer: It reports no dated signal and drafts a role-specific version. It must not invent an event, date, or personal observation.

faq.question: Can it guarantee inbox placement or legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. Published DNS records do not prove message authentication or inbox placement. Provider rules and regional marketing laws require current checks.

faq.question: What data does the optional Revnu preview receive?
faq.answer: After consent, the preview request includes only the public website URL, plus a skill-version header. It excludes secrets, code, drafts, and contact lists.
